title: Time words, tag questions and verb patterns

blurb.en: Travel through time words, add tag questions and match verbs with -ing or to.
blurb.vi: Du hành cùng từ chỉ thời gian, thêm câu hỏi đuôi và ghép động từ với -ing hoặc to.

title.vi: Động từ, câu hỏi và câu mệnh lệnh

already.def: Before now, or sooner than you think.
already.ex: I have *already* eaten my lunch, so I can play now.

yet.vi: chưa (dùng cuối câu hỏi và câu phủ định)
yet.def: Up to now. It goes at the end of questions and 'not' sentences.

ever.def: At any time in your life. We use it in questions.
ever.ex: Have you *ever* seen a shooting star?

never.vi: không bao giờ, chưa bao giờ
never.def: Not at any time. Not even one time.
never.ex: I have *never* been on a plane.

always.ex: I *always* brush my teeth before bed.

usually.def: Most of the time, but not every time.

sometimes.def: On some days, but not on other days.
sometimes.ex: I *sometimes* walk to school with my cousin.

hardly ever.def: Almost not at all. Only once in a long time.

enjoy.def: To like doing something a lot. The next verb ends in -ing.

hope.def: To want something good to happen. Then use to + a verb.
hope.ex: We *hope* to win the match on Saturday.

tag question.def: A very short question at the end of a sentence, like 'isn't it?'
tag question.ex: 'You like mango, don't you?' is a *tag question*.

instruction.vi: câu chỉ dẫn, câu mệnh lệnh
instruction.def: A sentence that tells someone what to do or what not to do.
instruction.ex: The first *instruction* on the card says 'Close the door.'

purpose.def: The reason why you do something. We often say it with to + a verb.
purpose.ex: The *purpose* of this box is to keep my pencils tidy.

title.vi: Từ chỉ thời gian: cho đến bây giờ

scenes.head: A chat about a space book
scenes.html:
Isla: Have you *ever* seen a shooting star?
Omar: No, I've *never* seen one. But I've *already* read a book about them!
Isla: Have you finished my space book *yet*?
Omar: Not *yet*. I *always* read before bed, but I'm only on page 20.
Isla: My brother *hardly ever* reads. He prefers football!

steps.en: *already* and *yet* go with have or has + a verb: I've *already* read it. Have you finished it *yet*?
steps.vi: *already* và *yet* đi với have hoặc has + động từ: I've *already* read it. Have you finished it *yet*?

steps.en: *already* = before now. It goes in the middle. *yet* goes at the end of questions and 'not' sentences.
steps.vi: *already* = đã rồi, trước bây giờ. Nó đứng ở giữa câu. *yet* đứng cuối câu hỏi và câu phủ định.

steps.en: *ever* asks about any time in your life. *never* means not one time.
steps.vi: *ever* hỏi về bất kỳ lúc nào trong đời. *never* nghĩa là chưa một lần nào.

steps.en: *always* and *hardly ever* say how often. *always* = every time. *hardly ever* = almost never.
steps.vi: *always* và *hardly ever* nói về mức độ thường xuyên. *always* = lúc nào cũng vậy. *hardly ever* = hầu như không bao giờ.

scenes.head: Mai and Grandma in the kitchen
scenes.html:
Grandma: These mangoes look sweet, *don't they*?
Mai: Yes! It's a hot day, *isn't it*? Let's make a mango drink.
Grandma: You can cut fruit, *can't you*?
Mai: Yes, I can. But this knife isn't very sharp, *is it*?
Grandma: No, it isn't. Be careful anyway!

steps.en: A *tag question* is a short question at the end of a sentence. We use it to check something or to ask someone to agree.
steps.vi: *Câu hỏi đuôi* là câu hỏi ngắn ở cuối câu. Ta dùng nó để kiểm tra điều gì đó hoặc để mong người nghe đồng ý.

steps.en: Positive sentence, negative tag: It's hot, *isn't it*? You can cut, *can't you*?
steps.vi: Câu khẳng định thì đuôi phủ định: It's hot, *isn't it*? You can cut, *can't you*?

steps.en: Negative sentence, positive tag: The knife isn't sharp, *is it*?
steps.vi: Câu phủ định thì đuôi khẳng định: The knife isn't sharp, *is it*?

steps.en: Use the same helper verb: is and isn't, can and can't. With other verbs use do or does: They look sweet, *don't they*?
steps.vi: Dùng lại cùng trợ động từ: is và isn't, can và can't. Với động từ thường, dùng do hoặc does: They look sweet, *don't they*?

title.en: Verb patterns, to + verb and instructions
title.vi: Mẫu động từ, to + động từ và câu mệnh lệnh

scenes.head: A leaflet at the sports club
scenes.html:
KITE DAY AT THE SPORTS CLUB!
Do you *enjoy making* things? Would you *like to fly* your own kite? You can *learn to make* one here!
We use thin sticks *to make* the frame and paper *to make* the sail.
*Bring* a pencil and some glue. *Don't bring* scissors. We have lots.
We *hope to see* you on Saturday!

steps.en: Some verbs take *-ing* after them: *enjoy making*, *love flying*, *finish painting*.
steps.vi: Một số động từ đi với *-ing* phía sau: *enjoy making*, *love flying*, *finish painting*.

steps.en: Some verbs take *to* + a verb: *want to*, *hope to*, *learn to*, *would like to*.
steps.vi: Một số động từ đi với *to* + động từ: *want to*, *hope to*, *learn to*, *would like to*.

steps.en: *to* + a verb can also give the reason (the purpose): We use sticks *to make* the frame.
steps.vi: *to* + động từ cũng có thể nêu lý do (mục đích): We use sticks *to make* the frame.

steps.en: An instruction starts with the verb: *Bring* glue. For 'no', start with *Don't*: *Don't bring* scissors.
steps.vi: Câu mệnh lệnh bắt đầu bằng động từ: *Bring* glue. Để nói 'không được', bắt đầu bằng *Don't*: *Don't bring* scissors.

end.en: Now find the time words, tags and verb patterns on your own!
end.vi: Bây giờ con hãy tự tìm từ chỉ thời gian, câu hỏi đuôi và mẫu động từ nhé!

challenge.result: You spotted time words, tag questions and verb patterns!

v.q: Which sentence means 'not one time in my life'?
opts: I always see snow in winter.
whys: 'already' means it happened before now, so you have seen snow.
'always' means every time, so you see snow a lot.
v.hint: Find the word that means 'not at any time'.
v.worked: 'never' = not one time: 'I have never seen snow.'

v.q: Which question asks about any time in your life?
opts: Have you ever eaten a durian?
whys: 'always' asks how often, not about any time in your life.
'now' asks about this moment, not about your whole life.
v.hint: Which time word means 'at any time in your life'?
v.worked: 'ever' asks about any time in your life: 'Have you ever eaten a durian?'

v.q: Which sentence ends with a tag question?
opts: It isn't cold today at all.
whys: This is a normal question. A tag is a short question at the END of a sentence.
This is a sentence with no question at the end.
v.hint: Look for a short question after a comma at the end.
v.worked: '..., isn't it?' is a short question at the end of the sentence: a tag question.

v.q: Which sentence has the right tag?
whys: The sentence has 'can', so the tag needs 'can', not 'do'.
The sentence is positive, so the tag must be negative: can't.
v.hint: Find the helper verb in the sentence. Use the same one in the tag.
v.worked: 'can' in the sentence, so 'can't you?' in the tag.

v.q: Which sentence is right?
whys: After 'enjoy' we use -ing, not to + verb.
After 'enjoy' the next verb needs -ing.
v.hint: Which form comes after 'enjoy'?
v.worked: 'enjoy' + -ing: 'We enjoy flying kites.'

v.q: Which sentence is right?
opts: I hope to visit the museum.
whys: After 'hope' we use to + verb, not -ing.
After 'hope' we need 'to' before the verb.
v.hint: Which form comes after 'hope'?
v.worked: 'hope' + to + verb: 'I hope to visit the museum.'

v.q: Which sentence says WHY with to + verb?
opts: I went to the shop to buy eggs.
I went to the shop with Dad.
I went to the shop on Monday.
whys: 'with Dad' says who, not why.
'on Monday' says when, not why.
v.hint: Look for to + a verb that gives a reason.
v.worked: 'to buy eggs' tells us why I went: it is the purpose.

v.q: Which sentence is an instruction?
opts: The pan is very hot now.
whys: This tells us what Grandma did. It doesn't tell anyone what to do.
This describes the pan. It doesn't tell anyone what to do.
v.hint: An instruction starts with a verb or with 'Don't'.
v.worked: 'Don't touch ...' starts with 'Don't': it tells you what not to do.

blurb.en: Practise one thing at a time: time words, tag questions, then verb patterns and instructions.
blurb.vi: Luyện từng phần một: từ chỉ thời gian, câu hỏi đuôi, rồi mẫu động từ và câu mệnh lệnh.

title.vi: Từ chỉ thời gian: already, yet, ever, never, always

v.q: I have ________ cleaned my room. Now I can play.
whys: 'yet' goes at the end of questions and 'not' sentences.
'ever' is for questions about any time in your life.
v.hint: Is this a question, a 'not' sentence or a 'yes' sentence?
v.worked: The room is clean before now: 'I have already cleaned my room.'

v.q: Have you finished your painting ________?
whys: 'never' doesn't go at the end of a question.
'always' says how often. It doesn't go at the end here.
v.hint: Which time word goes at the END of a question?
v.worked: 'yet' goes at the end of questions: 'Have you finished your painting yet?'

v.q: I have ________ been to the moon. Nobody in my class has!
whys: We don't use 'ever' in a 'yes' sentence like this one.
'already' means you have been there. Read the next sentence!
v.hint: Read the second sentence. Has anybody been to the moon?
v.worked: Nobody has been to the moon, so: 'I have never been to the moon.'

v.q: My grandpa has ________ used a computer. He doesn't know how!
whys: 'yet' goes at the end of 'not' sentences, not in the middle.
We don't use 'ever' in a 'yes' sentence like this one.
v.hint: Read the second sentence. Does he know how to use a computer?
v.worked: 'He doesn't know how' tells us: he has *never* used a computer.

v.q: Lena eats fruit every day. She ________ eats fruit.
whys: 'hardly ever' means almost never, but Lena eats fruit every day.
'never' means not one time, but Lena eats fruit every day.
v.hint: Every day means how often?
v.worked: 'every day' = always: 'She always eats fruit.'

v.q: Sam goes to the cinema once a year. He ________ goes.
whys: 'always' means every time, but Sam goes only once a year.
'never' means not one time, but Sam goes once a year.
v.hint: Once a year is not very often. Which words say that?
v.worked: Once a year is almost never: 'He hardly ever goes.'

v.q: It's very cold today, ________?
whys: The sentence is positive, so the tag must be negative.
The sentence has 'is' (it's), so the tag uses 'is', not 'does'.
v.hint: Positive sentence, negative tag. Which helper verb is in 'It's'?
v.worked: 'It's' = it is. Positive sentence, so: 'isn't it?'

v.q: This old bungalow is very small, ________?
whys: The sentence is positive, so the tag must be negative.
The sentence has 'is', so the tag uses 'is', not 'does'.
v.hint: Find the helper verb. Is the sentence positive or negative?
v.worked: 'is very small' is positive, so the tag is 'isn't it?'

v.q: Write the missing word in the tag.
lines: Nina can ride a bike, {0} she?
v.hint: Find the helper verb in the sentence. The sentence is positive.
v.worked: 'can ride' is positive, so the tag is negative: 'can't she?'

v.q: Write the missing word in the tag.
lines: You don't like spicy food, {0} you?
v.hint: The sentence has 'don't'. It is negative, so the tag is positive.
v.worked: 'don't like' is negative, so the tag is positive: 'do you?'

v.q: They don't eat meat, ________?
whys: The sentence is negative (don't), so the tag must be positive.
The sentence has 'don't', so the tag uses 'do', not 'are'.
v.hint: Negative sentence, positive tag. Which helper verb is in the sentence?
v.worked: 'don't eat' is negative, so the tag is positive: 'do they?'

v.q: Leo plays football on Sundays, ________?
whys: 'plays' has no 'is', so we use does or doesn't in the tag.
The sentence is positive, so the tag must be negative.
v.hint: There is no helper verb. Use do or does. Positive or negative?
v.worked: 'Leo plays' = he does. Positive sentence, so: 'doesn't he?'

title.en: Verb patterns, to + verb and instructions
title.vi: Mẫu động từ, to + động từ và câu mệnh lệnh

v.q: I love ________ photos of the sky at night.
whys: After 'love' we can't use the base verb 'take' alone.
'took' is the past. After 'love' use -ing.
v.hint: What form comes after 'love'?
v.worked: 'love' + -ing: 'I love taking photos.'

v.q: We want ________ the space museum next week.
whys: After 'want' we use to + verb, not -ing.
After 'want' we need 'to' before the verb.
v.hint: What comes after 'want'?
v.worked: 'want' + to + verb: 'We want to visit the space museum.'

v.q: Dad went to the shop ________ some fish.
whys: We need 'to' before the verb to give the reason.
'bought' is the past, but we need to + verb for the reason.
v.hint: Why did Dad go? Use to + verb for a reason.
v.worked: The reason is 'to buy some fish': to + verb.

v.q: We use a torch ________ in the dark.
whys: We need 'to' before the verb to say what the torch is for.
'saw' is the past. Use to + verb to say what it is for.
v.hint: What is a torch for? Use to + verb.
v.worked: A torch is for seeing: 'We use a torch to see in the dark.'

v.q: ________ the door when you go out, please.
whys: An instruction starts with the base verb, not -ing.
'Closed' is the past. An instruction starts with the base verb.
v.hint: An instruction starts with the verb. Which form?
v.worked: Instructions start with the base verb: 'Close the door.'

v.q: The pan is hot! ________ touch it.
whys: To say 'no' in an instruction, start with 'Don't', not 'Not'.
'Doesn't' is for he or she. Instructions use 'Don't'.
v.hint: How does a 'no' instruction start?
v.worked: A negative instruction starts with 'Don't': 'Don't touch it.'

blurb.en: Exam practice: circle the word, choose the best reply, then fill the gaps in a story.
blurb.vi: Luyện thi: khoanh tròn từ đúng, chọn câu trả lời phù hợp nhất, rồi điền chỗ trống trong bài kể chuyện.

v.q: My sister has ________ finished her new book. She is very fast!
whys: 'yet' goes at the end of questions and 'not' sentences.
We don't use 'ever' in a 'yes' sentence like this.
v.hint: Is the sentence a question, a 'not' sentence or a 'yes' sentence?
v.worked: She finished before now: 'has already finished'.

v.q: The rice isn't ready ________. Please wait ten more minutes.
whys: 'already' goes in 'yes' sentences, but this sentence has 'isn't'.
'ever' is for questions about any time in your life.
v.hint: The sentence has 'isn't'. Which word goes at the end of a 'not' sentence?
v.worked: 'isn't ready yet' = not ready up to now. 'yet' goes at the end.

v.q: The stars are very bright tonight, ________?
whys: The sentence is positive, so the tag must be negative.
The sentence has 'are', so the tag uses 'are', not 'do'.
v.hint: Find the helper verb. Positive sentence, negative tag.
v.worked: 'The stars are' is positive, so the tag is 'aren't they?'

v.q: Your brother doesn't eat mushrooms, ________?
whys: The sentence is negative (doesn't), so the tag must be positive.
The sentence has 'doesn't', so the tag uses 'does', not 'is'.
v.hint: Negative sentence, positive tag. Which helper verb is in the sentence?
v.worked: 'doesn't eat' is negative, so the tag is 'does he?'

v.q: Chloe would like ________ a yurt in Mongolia one day.
whys: After 'would like' we use to + verb, not -ing.
After 'would like' we need 'to' + the base verb.
v.hint: What comes after 'would like'?
v.worked: 'would like' + to + verb: 'would like to visit'.

v.q: Have you finished ________ your bedroom? Then you can go out.
whys: After 'finish' we use -ing, not to + verb.
After 'finish' the next verb needs -ing.
v.hint: What form comes after 'finish'?
v.worked: 'finish' + -ing: 'Have you finished tidying your bedroom?'

title.vi: Phần 2: chọn câu trả lời phù hợp nhất

v.q: "Have you tidied your room yet?" Choose the best reply.
opts: Yes, I'm going to start it.
No, I finished it last night.
whys: 'Yes' and 'going to start' don't match: if you haven't started, the answer is no.
'No' and 'I finished it' don't match.
v.hint: The question is about up to now. Check that 'Yes' or 'No' matches the rest of the reply.
v.worked: 'Have you tidied it yet?' 'Yes, I've already finished it.' Yes and already match.

v.q: "Have you ever been to a chocolate factory?" Choose the best reply.
opts: No, never. I'd love to go!
Yes, I'm going there next week.
whys: 'next week' is the future. The question asks about any time up to now.
'No' and 'I've already been there' don't match.
v.hint: 'ever' asks about any time in your life. Which reply answers that and makes sense?
v.worked: 'Have you ever ...?' 'No, never.' Then 'I'd love to go' makes sense.

v.q: "What would you like to do this weekend?" Choose the best reply.
opts: I'd like to go to the zoo.
I liked the zoo a lot.
I go to the zoo by bus.
whys: This is about the past. The question asks about this weekend.
This says how you go, not what you would like to do.
v.hint: The question asks about the future. Which reply uses 'would like' too?
v.worked: 'What would you like to do?' 'I'd like to go to the zoo.'

v.q: "Do you enjoy cooking with your dad?" Choose the best reply.
opts: Yes, we love making noodles together.
No, I cooked rice last week.
whys: This says where Dad is, not if you enjoy cooking.
This is about one time last week. The question is about what you enjoy.
v.hint: The question asks how you feel about cooking. Which reply says that?
v.worked: 'Do you enjoy cooking?' 'Yes, we love making noodles.' love + -ing answers it.

v.q: "Why are you taking a torch tonight?" Choose the best reply.
opts: To look at the stars outside.
whys: This says when, but the question asks why.
This says who with, but the question asks why.
v.hint: The question starts with 'Why'. Which reply gives a reason?
v.worked: 'Why?' 'To look at the stars.' to + verb gives the reason.

v.q: "I've got a bad cough. What should I do?" Choose the best reply.
opts: I hardly ever get a cough.
whys: This is about me, not advice for my friend.
This talks about yesterday. It doesn't say what to do.
v.hint: Your friend wants advice. Which reply tells them what to do?
v.worked: Advice is an instruction: 'Drink warm water and rest.'

title.vi: Phần 4: điền chỗ trống trong bài kể chuyện

v.q: Read the story. Gap (1): choose the word.
whys: We need to + verb to say why we took the bus.
'got' is the past, but after 'took a bus' we need to + verb for the reason.
v.hint: Why did they take a bus? Use to + verb for a reason.
v.worked: 'We took a bus to get there': to + verb gives the reason.

stim.head: A story by Ravi
stim.html:
Our trip to the space museum
Last Friday, my class went to the space museum. We took a bus (1) ________ there. First, we saw a real rover. It was huge! Then we went into a small room with a moon rock. I enjoyed (2) ________ the moon rock the most. It was cold and very heavy! I have (3) ________ wanted to go to space, and now I want it even more.

v.q: Read the story. Gap (1): choose the word.
whys: We need to + verb to say why I went to Grandma's house.
'helped' is the past, but we need to + verb for the reason.
v.hint: Why did Mai go to Grandma's house? Use to + verb for a reason.
v.worked: 'I went to Grandma's house to help her': to + verb gives the reason.

stim.head: A story by Mai
stim.html:
Spring rolls with Grandma
On Sunday, I went to Grandma's house (1) ________ her cook lunch. We made spring rolls. Grandma said, 'Be careful, and (2) ________ touch the hot oil!' Then I learned (3) ________ the rice paper. It was hard at first, but Grandma helped me. Our spring rolls were delicious. I hope to make them again soon.

v.q: Read the story. Gap (2): choose the word.
whys: After 'enjoy' we use -ing, not to + verb.
After 'enjoy' the next verb needs -ing.
v.hint: Look at the word before the gap: 'enjoyed'.
v.worked: 'enjoyed' + -ing: 'I enjoyed touching the moon rock.'

v.q: Read the story. Gap (2): choose the word.
whys: To say 'no' in an instruction, use 'don't', not 'not'.
'doesn't' is for he or she. Instructions use 'don't'.
v.hint: Grandma is giving an instruction. How does a 'no' instruction start?
v.worked: A negative instruction: 'don't touch the hot oil!'

It was hard at first, but Grandma helped me. Our spring rolls were delicious. I hope to make them again soon.

v.q: Read the story. Gap (3): choose the word.
whys: 'already' doesn't fit with 'wanted'. Read the end of the sentence: he still wants it.
'yet' goes at the end of 'not' sentences and questions.
v.hint: Read to the end of the sentence. Has he wanted it for a long time?
v.worked: 'I have always wanted ... and now I want it even more': all the time, up to now.

v.q: Read the story. Gap (3): choose the word.
whys: After 'learn' we use to + verb, not -ing.
'folded' is the past. After 'learn' we need to + verb.
v.hint: Look at the word before the gap: 'learned'.
v.worked: 'learn' + to + verb: 'I learned to fold the rice paper.'

items.en: *already* = before now. It goes after have or has. *yet* goes at the end of questions and 'not' sentences.
items.vi: *already* = đã rồi, trước bây giờ. Nó đứng sau have hoặc has. *yet* đứng cuối câu hỏi và câu phủ định.

items.en: *ever* asks about any time in your life. *never* = not one time.
items.vi: *ever* hỏi về bất kỳ lúc nào trong đời. *never* = chưa một lần nào.

items.en: How often? *always* (every time), *usually*, *sometimes*, *hardly ever* (almost never), *never* (not one time).
items.vi: Bao lâu một lần? *always* (lúc nào cũng vậy), *usually* (thường thường), *sometimes* (thỉnh thoảng), *hardly ever* (hầu như không), *never* (không bao giờ).

items.en: Tag questions: positive sentence + negative tag; negative sentence + positive tag. Use the same helper verb (is, are, can). No helper verb? Use do or does.
items.vi: Câu hỏi đuôi: câu khẳng định + đuôi phủ định; câu phủ định + đuôi khẳng định. Dùng lại cùng trợ động từ (is, are, can). Không có trợ động từ thì dùng do hoặc does.
example: It's sunny, *isn't it*? You can't swim, *can you*?
You like mango, *don't you*? He doesn't eat meat, *does he*?

items.en: After *enjoy*, *love* and *finish* use *-ing*. After *want*, *hope*, *learn* and *would like* use *to* + verb.
items.vi: Sau *enjoy*, *love* và *finish* dùng *-ing*. Sau *want*, *hope*, *learn* và *would like* dùng *to* + động từ.
example: I *want to go* home. We *would like to help*.

items.en: Use *to* + verb to say why (the purpose). Start an instruction with the verb; use *Don't* to say 'no'.
items.vi: Dùng *to* + động từ để nói vì sao (mục đích). Câu mệnh lệnh bắt đầu bằng động từ; dùng *Don't* để nói 'không được'.

check.sentence: I have {already|yet|ever} done my homework, so I can play.
We have {never|ever|yet} been to Da Lat. We'd love to go!
We {hardly ever|always|ever} eat fish. Only on my birthday!
Your dad works in a bank, {doesn't he|isn't he|does he}?
We use a net {to catch|catching|catch} fish.

v.q: Lena hasn't packed her school bag ________. The bus comes soon!
whys: 'already' goes in 'yes' sentences, but this sentence has 'hasn't'.
'ever' is for questions about any time in your life.
v.hint: The sentence has 'hasn't'. Which word goes at the end of a 'not' sentence?
v.worked: 'hasn't packed ... yet' = not up to now. 'yet' goes at the end.

v.q: Bao has ________ fed the cat, so it's sleeping now.
whys: 'yet' goes at the end of questions and 'not' sentences.
We don't use 'ever' in a 'yes' sentence like this.
v.hint: Is it a question, a 'not' sentence or a 'yes' sentence?
v.worked: He fed the cat before now: 'Bao has already fed the cat.'

v.q: The moon is very bright tonight, ________?
whys: The sentence is positive, so the tag must be negative.
The sentence has 'is', so the tag uses 'is', not 'does'.
v.hint: Positive sentence, negative tag. Which helper verb is in the sentence?
v.worked: 'The moon is' is positive, so the tag is 'isn't it?'

v.q: Sam can swim very well, ________?
whys: The sentence is positive, so the tag must be negative.
The sentence has 'can', so the tag uses 'can', not 'does'.
v.hint: Find the helper verb. Use the same one in the tag.
v.worked: 'can swim' is positive, so the tag is 'can't he?'

v.q: Your parents don't drink coffee, ________?
whys: The sentence is negative (don't), so the tag must be positive.
The sentence has 'don't', so the tag uses 'do', not 'are'.
v.hint: Negative sentence, positive tag. Which helper verb is in the sentence?
v.worked: 'don't drink' is negative, so the tag is 'do they?'

v.q: Nina isn't at home today, ________?
whys: The sentence is negative (isn't), so the tag must be positive.
The sentence has 'isn't', so the tag uses 'is', not 'does'.
v.hint: Negative sentence, positive tag. Which helper verb is in the sentence?
v.worked: 'isn't at home' is negative, so the tag is 'is she?'

v.q: My cousins enjoy ________ in the river in summer.
whys: After 'enjoy' we use -ing, not to + verb.
After 'enjoy' the next verb needs -ing.
v.hint: What form comes after 'enjoy'?
v.worked: 'enjoy' + -ing: 'My cousins enjoy swimming.'

v.q: Omar hopes ________ a famous runner one day.
whys: After 'hope' we use to + verb, not -ing.
After 'hope' we need 'to' before the verb.
v.hint: What comes after 'hope'?
v.worked: 'hope' + to + verb: 'Omar hopes to be a famous runner.'

v.q: We put a blanket on the sofa ________ it clean.
whys: We need to + verb to say why we put the blanket there.
'keeps' is the present simple. For a reason use to + verb.
v.hint: Why is the blanket there? Use to + verb for a reason.
v.worked: The reason is 'to keep it clean': to + verb.

v.q: Chloe used a big box ________ a space rocket.
whys: We need to + verb to say why Chloe used the box.
'makes' is the present simple. For a reason use to + verb.
v.hint: Why did Chloe use the box? Use to + verb for a reason.
v.worked: The reason is 'to make a space rocket': to + verb.

v.q: "Have you ever tried mango ice cream?" Choose the best reply.
opts: No, but I'd love to try it!
whys: 'tomorrow' is the future. The question asks about any time up to now.
'No' and 'I've already eaten it' don't match.
v.hint: 'ever' asks about any time in your life. Check that the reply makes sense.
v.worked: 'Have you ever tried it?' 'No, but I'd love to try it!' No and love to try match.

v.q: "Has your mum bought the birthday cake yet?" Choose the best reply.
opts: No, she's going to buy it later.
Yes, she's going to buy it.
No, she bought it this morning.
whys: 'Yes' and 'going to buy it' don't match: if she hasn't bought it, the answer is no.
'No' and 'she bought it' don't match.
v.hint: Check that 'Yes' or 'No' matches the rest of the reply.
v.worked: 'Has she bought it yet?' 'No, she's going to buy it later.' No and later match.

v.q: "Why do you need some string?" Choose the best reply.
opts: To make a kite with my brother.
It's in the box under my bed.
whys: This says where the string is, not why you need it.
This says how long, not why you need it.
v.hint: The question starts with 'Why'. Which reply gives a reason?
v.worked: 'Why?' 'To make a kite.' to + verb gives the reason.

v.q: "What's that big umbrella for?" Choose the best reply.
opts: It's to keep us dry in the rain.
It's from the shop near school.
whys: This says where it is from, not what it is for.
This says what it looks like, not what it is for.
v.hint: 'What's it for?' asks for a use. Look for to + verb.
v.worked: 'What's it for?' 'It's to keep us dry.' to + verb tells the use.

v.q: "It's a lovely sunny day, isn't it?" Choose the best reply.
opts: Yes, it is. Let's go outside!
Yes, I do. It's very warm.
No, it isn't. It's warm and sunny!
whys: The question has 'is', so we answer 'Yes, it is', not 'I do'.
'No, it isn't' does not match 'It's warm and sunny!'
v.hint: Look at the helper verb in the tag. Use it in your short answer.
v.worked: '..., isn't it?' 'Yes, it is.' The reply uses 'is' and agrees.

v.q: "You've got a pet cat, haven't you?" Choose the best reply.
opts: Yes, I have. She's called Snow.
Yes, I am. She's very small.
No, I haven't. She's black and white.
whys: The tag uses 'have', so we answer 'Yes, I have', not 'I am'.
'No, I haven't' does not match 'She's black and white.'
v.hint: Look at the helper verb in the tag. Use it in your short answer.
v.worked: '..., haven't you?' 'Yes, I have.' Then the reply tells us about the cat.

v.q: Read the story. Gap (1): choose the word.
whys: With the light on, it is harder to see the stars. Read the next sentence.
If they don't turn it off, they can't see the stars better.
v.hint: Read the sentence after the gap: 'Then we can see the stars better!'
v.worked: A dark garden is better for stars: 'Turn off the kitchen light.'

stim.head: A story by Leo
stim.html:
Stars in the garden
Last Saturday, I stayed at Grandpa's house. After dinner, we went into the garden to look at the stars. Grandpa said, '(1) ________ the kitchen light. Then we can see the stars better!' Grandpa knows the names of lots of constellations. He (2) ________ forgets them, even the difficult ones! Then we saw a shooting star. I want to stay with Grandpa again soon.

v.q: Read the story. Gap (1): choose the word.
whys: If she always eats cake, 'but she bought two pieces' is not a surprise.
If she usually eats cake, 'but' does not make sense.
v.hint: Look at 'but' after the gap. What is the surprise?
v.worked: 'hardly ever eats cake, but she bought two pieces': 'but' shows a surprise.

stim.head: A story by Chloe
stim.html:
Our cake sale
On Friday, our class had a cake sale to raise money for a class trip. We made chocolate cakes and lemon cakes. Parents and teachers came to buy them. Our teacher (1) ________ eats cake, but she bought two pieces! We sold every cake in one hour. We haven't counted the money (2) ________, so we don't know how much we made.

v.q: Read the story. Gap (2): choose the word.
whys: Grandpa knows the names, so he doesn't always forget them.
We don't use 'ever' in a 'yes' sentence like this.
v.hint: Read the sentence before: 'Grandpa knows the names'. Does he forget them?
v.worked: He knows them all, 'even the difficult ones': he never forgets them.

stim.head: A story by Leo
stim.html:
Stars in the garden
Last Saturday, I stayed at Grandpa's house. After dinner, we went into the garden to look at the stars. Grandpa said, '(1) ________ the kitchen light. Then we can see the stars better!' Grandpa knows the names of lots of constellations. He (2) ________ forgets them, even the difficult ones! Then we saw a shooting star. I want to stay with Grandpa again soon.

v.q: Read the story. Gap (2): choose the word.
whys: 'already' goes in 'yes' sentences, but this sentence has 'haven't'.
'ever' is for questions about any time in your life.
v.hint: Read to the end: 'so we don't know how much we made'.
v.worked: 'haven't counted ... yet' = not up to now, so they don't know how much.

stim.head: A story by Chloe
stim.html:
Our cake sale
On Friday, our class had a cake sale to raise money for a class trip. We made chocolate cakes and lemon cakes. Parents and teachers came to buy them. Our teacher (1) ________ eats cake, but she bought two pieces! We sold every cake in one hour. We haven't counted the money (2) ________, so we don't know how much we made.

items: I need a pen ___ a letter.
First ___ the box, then look inside.
We ___ eat sweets. Only on holidays.
He ___ brushes his teeth. Every night!
We went to the field ___ football.
Positive sentence, so the tag is ___.
Why did you go out? ___ buy milk.

goals: use already, yet, ever, never, always and hardly ever
add the right tag question: isn't it?, can't she?, do they?
choose -ing or to + verb after enjoy, love, want, hope and learn
use to + verb for a reason and give instructions with Don't
